# My plan for this year

Alright, let me think about this year's crops. I'm 73, been doing this since I was a boy with my father. Things have changed a lot but I still do most things the way I learned.

## My fields

I have 10.1 mu total. I split it like this, same as the last few years:
- **3 mu cotton** on the piece further from the house — that land has been cotton for many years, the soil suits it
- **7.1 mu wheat-maize** double-crop on the better land close by, that's our main food and income

I know some neighbors dropped cotton because the price is no good and picking is hard work. My two boys work in town most of the year, so picking is a problem for me too. My wife and daughter-in-law help, and my grandchildren when school is out. I thought about dropping cotton this year but my wife said we should keep some — we've always had cotton, and if wheat price is bad one year, cotton gives us something else. So three mu, a little less than before.

## Wheat (already in the ground, planted last October)

I planted around October 10-12, same as every year. Used seed I bought at the agricultural supply shop — Jimai variety, the one the shop owner sold to most of us in the village. About 30 yuan a mu for seed.

Before planting I put down compound fertilizer — two bags of the 15-15-15 on each mu, that's about 40 kg. That's my base. I'll topdress urea at the green-up stage in spring — one bag (40 kg) covers roughly three mu, so about 13-14 kg urea per mu. If the wheat looks yellow I'll add more, but I usually don't need to.

Water: I irrigate at green-up, then again at jointing if no rain, then once more at grain-filling. Usually three times. Last year I did four because it was dry. The well is mine to share with two other households, we take turns. Pumping electricity costs money, each round is maybe 25 yuan per mu.

Weeds I spray once in early spring, herbicide from the shop, nothing complicated. Aphids sometimes at heading — if I see them I spray insecticide, if not I don't.

Last year wheat gave me about 420 kg/mu. I expect similar this year. I don't aim for 500 — that's for the farmers with bigger fields and more money for fertilizer. 400+ is good enough for us.

## Maize (right after wheat in June)

As soon as the wheat is cut — usually around June 10-12 — we have to move fast. My neighbor with the machine helps me; I pay him to harvest wheat and drill maize directly into the stubble. No real tillage, just direct seeding. This is the only way when the window is one week.

Seed: hybrid maize, Zhengdan or whatever the shop has, about 50 yuan a mu. I plant dense, the way we do now.

Fertilizer: I put compound fertilizer down with the planter — one bag per 1.5 mu, so maybe 25 kg compound at seeding. Then I topdress urea at the big trumpet stage (大喇叭口), about half a bag per mu, around 15-18 kg urea. That's about 10-12 kg N/mu total with what's in the compound. Neighbors apply similar.

Water: if the rains come in July-August like normal, I don't irrigate maize. If it's dry at tasseling, I'll pump once. Usually one irrigation, sometimes none.

Pesticide: herbicide right after planting, and I look for borers — if bad I spray once. 

Yield: I get around 450-480 kg/mu on maize most years. Good land, and the hybrids are strong now.

## Cotton (planted late April)

Cotton I've been planting around April 20-25 for decades. Covered with film (地膜) to warm the soil — it's extra work but it helps. Seed is not cheap, maybe 60 yuan a mu for the pest-resistant kind.

Fertilizer: cotton takes less than maize in my experience. I put one bag compound per mu at planting (15 kg), and if the plants look weak I side-dress urea at flowering, maybe 10 kg/mu. Total nitrogen around 10-12 kg/mu.

Water: cotton I irrigate once or twice — at budding and at boll-setting if dry. Once usually.

Pests: cotton has many pests, bollworm mostly. Even the pest-resistant seed I still spray 2-3 times for other bugs. Herbicide once or twice. This is where the money goes on cotton.

Picking: this is my biggest headache. My wife, daughter-in-law and me do most of it. We pick 3-4 times from September through October. If it's a big year I hire some help from the village for a few days. Last year I paid about 100 yuan per day for two helpers for a week.

Yield: I get about 250 kg lint per mu. Price has been poor — maybe 6 yuan per kg dry seed cotton. It barely pays but we keep doing it.

## Total costs and worry

Let me add it up roughly. For all 10.1 mu, fertilizer, seed, pesticide, irrigation, film, some hired labor for cotton — maybe 4,500-5,000 yuan total for the year. I have some savings from last year's harvest and my boys send money sometimes. I'll be okay but I don't have money to waste.

I won't try anything new this year. At my age, I do what works. If the extension man comes and tells me something, I listen, but I don't change what I've done for fifty years just because somebody says to.
